Problem.content: Penelitian ini mengevaluasi dua pendekatan peningkatan performa LLM, yaitu fine-tuning dan retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), untuk mendukung pengambilan keputusan hukum dalam konteks pajak pertambahan nilai (VAT).
Problem.quote: Methods This study experimentally evaluates two common approaches for enhancing LLM performance—fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)

Domain & Data.content: Domainnya adalah pajak nilai tambah (VAT) di Austria/EU, menggunakan kasus VAT dari buku teks serta kasus nyata dari firma konsultan pajak; bahasa tidak disebut.
Domain & Data.quote: applied to both textbook VAT cases and real-world cases from a tax consulting firm

Main Results.content: LLM yang dikonfigurasi dengan tepat dapat secara efektif mendukung profesional pajak dalam tugas-tugas VAT, mengotomatisasi pekerjaan rutin, dan menghasilkan justifikasi hukum yang kuat.
Main Results.quote: Properly configured LLMs can effectively support tax professionals in VAT-related tasks, automating routine work, providing initial analyses, and generating legally grounded justifications for decisions

Limitations.content: Prototipe belum siap untuk otomatisasi penuh karena sensitivitas domain hukum, serta masih terdapat keterbatasan dalam menangani pengetahuan implisit klien dan dokumentasi kontekstual.
Limitations.quote: current prototypes are not yet ready for full automation given the sensitivity of the legal domain, and limitations persist in handling implicit client knowledge and context-specific documentation

Gap.content: Inferensi: Makalah ini tidak membahas faithfulness atau abstention pada sistem RAG, tidak menggunakan dokumen perbankan berbahasa Indonesia, sehingga tidak menjawab fokus penelitian yang menilai kemampuan RAG dalam konteks tersebut.
Gap.quote: LLMs show strong potential to assist tax consultants by reducing workload and supporting VAT decision-making

Problem.text: Background Tax consulting clients often describe cases in natural language, making large language models (LLMs) attractive for supporting legal decision-making in Austrian and EU value-added tax (VAT) law. However, the requirement for legally grounded, well-justified analyses is challenged by LLMs’ propensity to hallucinate.Methods This study experimentally evaluates two common approaches for enhancing LLM performance—fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)—applied to both textbook VAT cases and real-world cases from a tax consulting firm. The aim is to identify optimal configurations of LLM-based systems and assess their legal-reasoning capabilities.Results Properly configured LLMs can effectively support tax professionals in VAT-related tasks, automating routine work, provid

LLMs can effectively support tax professionals in VAT-related tasks, automating routine work, providing initial analyses, and generating legally grounded justifications for decisions. However, current prototypes are not yet ready for full automation given the sensitivity of the legal domain, and limitations persist in handling implicit client knowledge and context-specific documentation.Conclusion LLMs show strong potential to assist tax consultants by reducing workload and supporting VAT decision-making, though future work should focus on integrating structured background information to address remaining gaps in contextual understanding.
